text:
Maria: Heads up — seeing intermittent NaNs in prod when serving mixed-precision matmul on long-context requests (~6k tokens). Happens after warmup when the kernel selector flips between fp16 and fp8 for adjacent batches.

Sam: Can you share a minimal repro + exact flags you used?

Maria: Repro command I used locally:```./bin/serve_infer --model=open-llm-v2 --seq_len=6144 --quant=fp8_auto --kv_mode=packed --batching=dynamic --profile=everything``` Logs show: 
```
[2026-03-02 09:12:01] kernel_selector: selected fp8_matmul_v2 for batch_size=2 seq=512
[2026-03-02 09:12:05] kernel_selector: switched to fp16_matmul for batch_size=1 seq=1024
[2026-03-02 09:12:05] runtime: floating point exception (core dumped) in matmul_kernel.cu:line 412
```
Corruption appears only when switch happens mid-stream and KV cache is enabled (packed mode).

Sam: Does the KV padding / stride calculation change when you merge batches? Might be an alignment bug when we reuse packed buffers. @Kyle any ideas?

Kyle: Yep — saw something similar in a fuzzer run last month. When two requests with different prefix lengths are co-batched we pad to the max prefix but the packed-kv stride calc was using the _previous_ kernel's element size in one codepath. On kernel switch the stride wasn't recomputed before the memcpy. That yields misaligned KV offsets and NaNs on fp8 dequant paths.

Jason: Quick repro I used (python):```python
# send two concurrent requests with different prefix_len
client.send_request(text='A'*1000, prefix_len=1000)
client.send_request(text='B'*6000, prefix_len=6000)
# force dynamic batching with small delay to encourage co-batch
time.sleep(0.01)
```
With that pattern the fp8 path flips and we get NaNs ~1/20 runs.

Maria: Profiling notes: matmul kernel alone: fp8 path is ~1.8x faster than fp16 for large seqs. But for short/heterogeneous seqs the quantize/dequant overhead and calibration-table lookup costs make fp8 only ~1.05x faster or even slower. Also saw a weird perf regression when the calibration-table cache grows: calibration lookup added ~10-20\% overhead when not reused.

Sam: So we have two issues: correctness (KV stride + kernel switch) and a perf footgun (calibration table lookup + per-batch quant overhead). Proposed fixes: 1) Always recompute and validate KV stride when kernel selection changes. 2) Introduce a small per-worker calibration-table cache keyed by (model, dtype-profile, seq_bucket) and reuse across adjacent batches. 3) Add CI fuzzer that mixes prefix lengths and forces kernel flips.

Kyle: I'll open a PR for the stride recompute + assert replay. Plan: recompute_strides_on_kernel_switch(), add an invariant check in debug builds, and add a test that co-batches variable prefix lengths. Assigning to me and Maria.

Kyle: Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1489 (WIP) — adds:
- recompute_stride_on_kernel_switch()
- debug assert that packed_kv_offset % element_size == 0
- small stress test that runs 500 co-batch cases with randomized prefix lengths

Maria: I can add the calibration cache patch (simple LRU per worker) and benchmark numbers. Early local runs: with cache enabled fp8 amortized perf goes from ~1.05x -> ~1.6x for mixed short/long workloads. Also removes pathological slowdowns.

deploy-bot: rolled back canary 2026-03-02T09:20:11Z due to increased error rate (revert of latest fp8 heuristics).

Sam: Good. Please include a telemetry event for kernel_switch + kv_stride_mismatch so we can monitor in prod. Also add a unit test that asserts no NaNs for 2000 randomized co-batches.

Jason: I'll help add the fuzzer harness to eng-tests and run it on the next nightly.

Maria: Adding logs and a minimal unit test now. Thanks — let's try to get the stride fix + cal-cache in canary by EOD. :thumbsup:
